//: The demo's own metadata, beside manifest.json and never inside it. manifest.json is the registry contract and must stay byte-identical in both plugin sources (app-shell BR-AS78); nothing here means anything to a registry. The lab shell reads this file through its own scan and nothing in it can admit a plugin, contribute a route or supply a remote.url (BR-AS79).

readiness.//: Asserted, not assumed. /readyz asks NATS for the log and both KV buckets on every call, so a shim that is up before `docker compose up` reports not ready rather than ready.

api.//: The command surface, route by route, so the lab shell can serve it on its own origin (app-shell BR-AS82). Embedded, the page is on the shell's origin and an absolute call to 20402 is cross-origin, so the browser discards the answer and every button reports `Failed to fetch`. The fix is the shell proxying these paths, NOT a wider CORS grant in cqrs/names.go — see this demo's CLAUDE.md and the phase's F-3. Every path here is also a route in cqrs/serve.go; a path not listed is not forwarded, which is what stops this being a general tunnel. /readyz is deliberately absent: it has its own route above, and it is the shell's call to make, not the page's. The trailing slash on /commands/ is a prefix, matching how serve.go registers it.

//runCommand: The WHOLE demo, not just its server (app-shell task 16k). Four processes have to be up before /readyz can answer yes: the NATS container, `cqrs serve` on 20402, and the snapshotter and projector that fill the two KV buckets. The old one-liner started only the container, so a reader who followed it was left with the same `unknown` the command was printed to fix. The script converges — it is safe to run again on a demo that is already up — and `deploy/stop.sh` reverses it.
